theGoodRide.title: K2 Excavator 2023-2026 Snowboard Review
theGoodRide.evidence: Review updated for 2026. Reviewer disclosed a three-day current demo on 150 and 154 plus prior days on the model, but the exact sample production year is not stated. Describes strong directional float for a short-wide, carving and speed as strong, soft uneven snow as good, hard uneven snow as a limitation, average switch/jib, usable jump/pop, and mid-tier glide relative to price. Not a separately verified 2027 test.

snowboardersJournalRideReview.title: K2 Excavator Unisex Snowboard
snowboardersJournalRideReview.author: Colin Wiseman
snowboardersJournalRideReview.sampleScope: One disclosed 154 cm sample. Tester is 5 ft 7 in, 155 lb, US boot size 8, with 31 years of riding experience. He rode it from Mt. Baker's mid-November opening day and says he added another half-dozen days after day two; article publication date, test season, and exact production year are not stated. The page credits photos to K2 Snowboarding.
snowboardersJournalRideReview.conditions: Opening day included deep, heavy, approximately 32-degree Cascadian powder, where the tester needed planing speed before steering from the center and reported back-leg fatigue. Later notes cover a bootpack-accessed backcountry day on consolidated snow, steep/fast turns, treed runouts, uneven terrain, pillow features, and resort groomers; exact dates and snow measurements are not given.
snowboardersJournalRideReview.observations: Reports strong edge hold on steep turns, lively feel and stability across undulating terrain, useful float after the wide nose reaches speed, quick carving, and a comfortable all-mountain/freeride character. The author suggests riding near usual board length for the deepest days. This adds qualitative support for short-wide float, speed/turn response, and moderate versatility, while the heavy-powder back-leg effort is an explicit limit.
snowboardersJournalRideReview.constructionCaveat: The review mentions bamboo stringers and a 20 mm taper, while the current official 2027 source describes ICG 10 Biax Glass with Carbon and Carbon Power Fork. Do not use the review to override or fill current-season construction fields; its production year is unknown.
snowboardersJournalRideReview.scoreUse: Directional corroboration only. No external numeric rating is mapped. Combined with The Good Ride's 2026 multi-day update, it supports the existing stability 8.0 and float 8.5 direction, but uncertain season, single rider, and no controlled comparison do not justify another score change. No reliable park-specific testing or price/value evidence is added.

skiEssentials2023Test.evidence: Multiple testers rode size 154. Reported strong stability and flotation, with mixed playfulness/forgiveness and differing fit impressions; not evidence of same-year 2027 performance.

observations.stability: Tracks well at speed and performs well in soft uneven snow; hard uneven snow can feel chattery/cranky.
observations.response: Strong committed carve and energetic return; edge-to-edge initiation depends on sizing and boot size.
observations.float: Very good directional float for a short-wide; reviewer says it is not their first choice as a dedicated powder board.
observations.park: Has pop for jumps and drops; reviewer does not prefer it for switch, and jib is not a specialty.
observations.forgiveness: Easy to skid and relatively non-hooky if sized appropriately; medium-to-medium-stiff feel and sizing/width are caveats.
observations.value: Reviewer calls base glide mid-tier and slower than competitors at this price.

skiEssentials2023Test.observations: Testers often scored stability and float positively; comments varied with rider size/fit, and one tester found it stiff, less playful and not very forgiving. Historical, non-2027 directional corroboration only.

scoringEvidence.siteScoreDecision: Update stability 8.5 -> 8.0 to reflect the specific hard-uneven-snow caveat while retaining strong groomer/soft-chop performance; update float 9.0 -> 8.5 because reviews describe strong short-wide float but stop short of dedicated-powder-board performance. The Snowboarder's Journal adds an 8+-day 154 cm single-rider account across heavy powder, backcountry, uneven snow and groomers, but does not disclose model year; its back-leg effort in heavy powder supports the existing non-specialist caveat without warranting another score change. Keep response 8.3, park 6.0 and forgiveness 6.8 as low-confidence editorial estimates; no external numeric score is linearly mapped. Keep value 7.4 provisionally and particularly uncertain: official US USD 629.95 and official Japan JPY 91,300 tax-inclusive are regional references only, not China-market prices; The Good Ride also criticizes glide for price.
scoringEvidence.confidence: low to moderate for riding direction, low for numerical site scores and value; no independently confirmed 2027 sample

seedMappingNotes: The official size list has six lengths (142/146/150/154/158/162), so there is no unique middle size. This pass does not choose a single representative length; all six official rows are stored in YAML sizeSpecs and this raw archive.
The K2 table's single Stance value is a reference stance, not a stance-width range. Source inches and converted display millimeters are retained together.
K2 lists setback as +0.75 inch toward the tail; the seed uses -19 mm according to its directional setback convention, with the exact official value preserved above.
No official board mass was found. Do not infer board weight from retailer shipping weights or review adjectives.
No China-market price source was found. CNY 4536 remains a project-rate normalization of official US $629.95, not a verified local price; value score remains low confidence.
